questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wished for my exchange to be in a big city, but with new cultures. I choose Milan over Bologna, due to it is more fun to be in the big city visiting the small city, than the other way around. I saw that by gong to Milan, you could easily travel to other cities as well. I also love italy because of the food, people, language and attitude!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I LOVED my exchange period. It has truly made me so grateful.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy once you accepted the fact that in Italy, everything moves more slowly. So I actually first got information about my school start and timetabels 1 week prior to the lessons starting.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Yes, Massimo Costa was the exchange coordinator at the university, and I also just wrote the professors or asked other exchange studnets, if I was in doubt of something.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I did'nt really need them, luckily :) But they were there!

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used the website HousingAnywhere to find my apartment, which I shared with three other Erasmus students. I would recommend the site, but they do charge an additional administration fee, which you will not get back. Although I found the apartment via HousingAnywhere, the rent payments were handled through ReBoutique.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is expensive in Milan, but it is manageable, I know of some who paid 5000 dkk for rent, I paid 6500 dkk. It is also a bit tricky to find apartments, so do start looking as soon as you are confirmed of exchange,

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not see any student accommodation..

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was okay :)

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register online at Unimia, where you also enroll in your courses. This allows you to access your timetable in Orari.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I think the same as in DK..

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 3/4 of the classes that I wished for before going. 1 of the courses were not available for my semester.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Maybe you should consider in the first week, attending more classes that you think you might want to have. I ended up changing 1 course along the way.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is apparent that Italian-English is something you need to learn, as well as the italian students being younger and speak italian whenever they can:)

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 3/4 of my courses were MA courses, they are not harder that the BA levels we are used to in DK:

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was more laid back and easy, than KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Programming for Social Data Science (MA)
2. Digital Society (MA)
3. Languages of the Media (BA)
4. Corporate Communication (MA)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I definitely recommend digital society and languages of the media, bot with Christopher Anderson - as professor. The courses are easy, fun and in digital you watch movies every friday as part of the course.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Hmmm our deposit for the apartment was 17.000 dkk each, which is quite a lot compared to what I heard from other students..

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transportation, and ATM card for students is 22 euros, and you get transportation all around Milan for 1 month, very little compared to DK. Also the food in supermarkets are better and cheaper, going out to eat is cheaper, coffee is like 1-2 euros, everything is cheaper.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not attend

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I dont know

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go meet people!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I think you should prioritise museums like fodazione Prada, og Mudec, as well as prioritise Chinatown and the cemetery Monumentale. I think you should go eat places like the locals, and maybe take some trips to either verona, torino, como, florence, vienezia.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, in Milan people are sweet and talkative.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Hmm maybe attend the Erasmus events, there are lots of them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Italian language, I recommend you learn basic conversation, just because not everyone knows English.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people, food, wine, going out, culture, everything

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Things like course registration, timetables, and paperwork can feel confusing and slow compared to UCPH. Systems like Unimia and Orari work… eventually... Register early, double-check deadlines, and don’t panic if things change last minute, that’s normal in Italy. Life in Milan runs differently than in Copenhagen: later dinners, long lunches, more social interaction, and a strong café culture. Professors may be less informal, but classmates are very social.
Finding accommodation in Milan can be stressful and expensive. Use platforms like HousingAnywhere, but be aware of non-refundable fees and always verify who you’re actually renting from.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just enjoy it BIG TIME. It is so fun, and time really flies.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The meeting new people, and having a successful living abroad.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Maybe accepting that money comes and go, and don't hold back on things you would like to experience.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Have fun :)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
